data.exact_reserve_text: An overall improvement of GBP 3.3 million on prior years' provisions was experienced during the year. This is due to improvements of GBP 3.6 million on property reinsurance and GBP 0.2 million on marine reinsurance partially offset by a deterioration of GBP 0.5 million on casualty reinsurance.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Material exposure to business interruption claims with significant uncertainty over ultimate costs, affecting 2019 and 2020 years of account.

prior_year_events.event_name: Australian BI legal test cases (Test Case 2 / appeals)
prior_year_events.impact_description: Outstanding legal rulings in Australia could materially affect liability for BI claims impacting the 2019 year of account.

named_events.loss_description: Severe winter storm and freeze in Texas causing around US$15bn of insured damage (industry figure).
Largest single loss event in 2021 with estimated total insured loss of around US$36bn (industry figure); largest natural peril loss incurred by the syndicate during 2021.
Extremely damaging flood in July causing around US$13bn of insured damage (industry figure).
Outbreak of tornadoes across the US Mid-West in December 2021.
Court case expected to challenge the basis upon which claims have been paid to date; cited as affecting the 2018 year of account closure.
Court case cited alongside CG Restaurants & Bars v RSA as potentially challenging claims payment bases.

data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2021 were GBP 106.65m. During 2021 there was an overall prior-year improvement (release) of GBP 3.3m on prior years' provisions, primarily driven by favourable development on property reinsurance (GBP 3.6m) and marine (GBP 0.2m) partially offset by adverse development on casualty (GBP 0.5m). COVID-19 related BI uncertainty and outstanding legal rulings continue to create reserve uncertainty for 2019 and earlier years.
